name: King of the South
overview: The King of the South is a male ruler identified as one of the four kings mentioned in Daniel 11:5. He is notably recognized as the King of Egypt, a significant political figure in the biblical prophecy. While his tribal affiliation is not specified, his role as a king places him prominently in the prophetic narrative.
namesAndTitles: The title 'King of the South' means 'prince of the south' and is used as a designation rather than a personal name. This title appears in Daniel 11:5 and is not given by God but serves to identify his geographical and political domain in the prophecy.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that the King of the South has a daughter, as referenced in Daniel 11:6. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are documented in the biblical text concerning this figure.
scriptureSignificance: The King of the South holds importance in the prophetic vision of Daniel 11 as one of the four kings who play key roles in the unfolding of God's sovereign plan. His identification as the King of Egypt situates him in the historical and prophetic conflict described in the passage. His interactions, including familial alliances such as the marriage of his daughter, contribute to the broader narrative of divine sovereignty over earthly kingdoms.
